A trip to Beijing isn't complete without a visit to the Forbidden City (紫禁城 - Zǐjìnchéng). This immense palace complex was built by Emperor Yongle between 1406 and 1420 by over a million workers. At 720,000 m², this iconic complex is the largest palace in the world (so allow plenty of time for a visit!). Legend has it that the complex has 9,999 rooms (one less than the perfect Celestial Palace), but a recent count revealed that there were "only" 8,886. The Forbidden City served as the residence of the 24 Ming and Qing emperors, their families, and their court, and was the ceremonial and political center of the Chinese government from 1420 to 1912/1924. When Puyi abdicated in 1912, he was allowed to continue living in the northern section (the Inner Court), while the southern section (the Outer Court) was already open to the public. After a coup in 1924, Puyi was finally evicted, and a year later, the Forbidden City became a museum. In the early 21st century, the Palace Museum carried out a major restoration to restore the Forbidden City to its pre-1911 state, with the goal of opening 76% of the palace to the public. Be sure to reserve tickets, because you will not be the only visitor. Nowadays, the Forbidden City receives an average of 40,000 visitors per day!

An absolute must go for your first visit to Beijing. To navigate the legions of local tourists and numerous entrances and checkpoints you should engage a tour guide through one of the online companies. A guide is also essential to understanding more of the history. We catered about 4hours walking tour and covered about 60% of the grounds, starting at Tiananmen and ending up at Jingshan Park (take the underpass, and pay for the separate entrance fee of 2 Chinese yuan)

My recent trip to the Palace Museum in Beijing was an imperial odyssey through time. Stepping through the Meridian Gate, the Forbidden City unfolded like a majestic dreamscape. Golden roofs shimmered beneath the azure sky, each tile whispering tales of dynasties past. I wandered through courtyards bathed in the hushed reverence of ancient guardians, their stone faces weathered by centuries of silent observation. Inside, throne rooms echoed with the phantom footsteps of emperors, their opulent décor a testament to vanished grandeur. My eyes feasted on exquisite porcelain treasures, intricate jade carvings, and vibrant silk tapestries, each brushstroke a brush with history. As the sun dipped behind the Jade Mountain, casting long shadows across the Forbidden City, I knew I had walked not just through a palace, but through a portal to a bygone era, leaving me forever enchanted by its splendor.

Definitely, that's the heart of Beijing City. A sample of World Heritage, preserved in a perfect shape as one of the best treasures of China legacies. If you can feel the spirit of this place, you can walk around the city, hidden in Forbidden City, in the era of Ming and Qing dynasties. A huge surface area, covered with buildings erected in a very particular and in the same time, traditional manner, extraordinary details and brilliant executed at their time. Unbelievable how they built a such big compound of building in a relatively few years. Definitely, this was an avant-garde complex at its time for entire world. Cannot miss this opportunity to visit this unique turistic spot. Tickets in advance and reservations are a must for your visit! Pay attention to this detail a couple of days before!

Amazing architecture with a rich history, from the 九钉门 (how only the royal doors will have 9 rows and 9 columns of 'nails') to the different functions of the various 宫殿 (太和殿，中和殿，保和殿，三宫六院) containing a total of 8,707 rooms, covering 150,000 sqm out of the 720,000 sqm premises. We entered through the middle door at 午门, which usually is used only by the Emperor, even the Empress can only enter through here once (on their wedding day, which are not many because usually most are already married before the Prince becomes Emperor). The top 3 scholars (科举的状元, 榜眼，探花) are also exceptions that are allowed to enter through the main door, once in their life when they make it to top 3 of the imperial exams. I enjoyed the place, it's breathtaking, despite the hazy weather, you can still the beauty of the architecture, the pure presence of the size (imagine how much they had to walk in the past and how they navigated this huge red-walled maze without Maps). The Emperor's throne was alttle underwhelming though, I had expected it to be bigger and more glamourous. Ended the day exiting through 神武门 after 2 hrs of walking in it.

The palace is so big. I was so impressed how people in the past could create this amazing works. Not to mention about the king, people who made such afford to support their respect, trust and love were so respectful. The palaces in the front seemed to be more beautiful from renovation while the latter are relatively aged (which is right!) There are a bit messy from crown at the entrance. We must fight with Chinese tourists as well

A really interesting point of destination. A must see if you are in Beijing, you can spend a whole day, but I do recommend some sort of guide to explain what you are looking at. Definitely not a "tourist trap." Really interesting as a large outside area which acts as one large museum. Seeing this is a great introduction to the rest of Beijing's palaces and helps fill in the timeline of china's rich history.

The Forbidden City of Beijing China. One of the coolest places I've ever been to. Full of history. Plenty of things to see. You can spend all day here if you wanted to. There is a really nice park located on the northern side after you exit. You'll have to climb a small mountain though to reach the top.

This is by far one of the most impressive places I visited in China. The Chinese history & culture was literally written on the walls. I (of course) couldn't read it but it was beautiful just the same. The rich colors & exemplary craftsmanship were just a couple of things that catch your eye as you walk through this behemoth of a palace. There were hundreds of people there but it didn't seem crowded as many places do. I listened to every word & read every word I could understand and my tour walked through over 2 hours and I could have spent much longer. They do have small gift shops inside and I couldn't help but pick up a few things for family back home and also myself of course. I strongly recommend visiting on your next trip to China.

Very popular and full of tourists, but don’t miss this attraction because of that. It’s popular for a reason. Historic grounds, sprawling courtyards and grand vistas of ancients buildings and cultures. Even with the crowds, you can sense it’s cultural impact on this ancient land. It is full of separate museums that are worth viewing, and you can spend as long as you want in each of them. There are guided tours, we opted to go without, and still were overwhelmed with sights and information. We spent about 4 hours here, but could have easily spent more time (or less, if you’re in a rush and don’t have half a day).

I planned my trip to the Forbidden City on TeaTeaLand. My trip planner suggested I bring a telephoto lens, as the Forbidden City can get very crowded. You probably won't be able to take any good pictures with a wide-angle lens. I'm so grateful for his advice, I took this set of beautiful pictures! The Forbidden City is really big, you must wear a pair of good shoes. I went to the Forbidden City around 3pm as my trip planner said, when there were fewer people than during the morning peak, and the sunlight was perfect for taking pictures. Thank you so much TeaTeaLand.

reviews.authorName: จิรารัตน์ ทัตติยกุล อ.
reviews.text: The ticket to the palace museum should be reserved on the palace website 7 days in advance. It is 60 CNY in the peak months + 10 cny for treasure gallerupy and 10 cny for clock gallery. If you reserve and pay in advance, just show your passport at the entrance. Do not need to get a paper ticket.

The Forbidden City is an impressive historic palace complex with grand halls, intricate architecture, and rich history. Walking through its courtyards and galleries offers a deep insight into China’s imperial past. A must-visit for history and culture lovers.
Must visit. Filled with history. Very large area and many buildings open to public to view. If possible I recommend a guide as there are many small and interesting informing on it.

The most impressive palace complex was built in 1420 by Ming emperor later used by Qing dynasty & was turned in nowadays The Palace Museum. There was a long queue & crowd at entrance, we had to undergo security checks. Nearly one thousand small & big traditional Chinese buildings with red walls & yellow roofs looked wonderful. A lot of wooden structures were used to build the buildings. Front side was used for ceremonies & state functions & backside was residency of royals. Security seemed very tight, palace was surrounded by 26 feet high huge walls, just outside the wall was a 20 feet deep & 170 feet wide ditch. Big courtyard, gardens, temples, halls & nearly ten thousand rooms in about one thousand building mase the palace complex a big city where ordinary people were not allowed hence forbidden city. A great place to visit while in Beijing.

Spent a whole day at the Forbidden City and still not enough time to visit all the places. So much history learnt and so many part is the palaces yet to be discovered. It’s more about getting an idea of what life was like at the Forbidden City rather than the fine details of the palace (e.g. actual room tour of one of the mini palaces etc) Definitely worth visiting when in Beijing!

Its magnificent and beautiful. Must sign up for a guided tour so all buildings make sense and learn abt the interesting history of this place. Ive visited during winter -12°..but it feels like more than -20° in the palace due to the wind and the snow on the ground in certain areas. Pls bring extra warm handgloves and socks. Wear comfortable insulated shoes..for a long walk.

The Palace Museum a.k.a the Forbidden City. As a Chinese arriving at this place literally gave me goose bumps. The sheer grandeur of the entrance gate itself blew me away. As you walk through the gate you can already feel the size of this place. The gate entrance alone is at least 10 feet deep. The restoration work put through here must have been laborious. If you have the flexibility of time and appreciate beauty and photography you need at least 2-3 hours here to slowly go as far as you are allowed to go. Make sure you are aware of the closing times and time it 3 hours backwards. The reason for this is as the closing time closes in the crowd thins out and you will be able appreciate the beauty of the place with less crowd. I was here early Dec and sunset is around 16:45 .. the golden light for photography is absolutely amazing The visit to The Forbidden City is one of the few good reasons to go to Beijing, this is a must definitely go.

A must-see for the architecture. This one location makes a lot of other smaller attractions redundant as you will have seen all of the core structural designs. If you're interested in the ticketed exhibitions, make sure you head to them with priority over the free exhibitions instead. You might not have enough time to cover the entire palace. Be prepared to allocate around 5-6 hours for your visit. There is a lot to take in once you're inside, so it's advisable to look up recommended travel routes. For foreigners, all you need is to bring your passport to the admissions booth. No reservation required. It costs 60 RMB for entry, and the ticketed exhibitions cost 10 RMB each, charged at the actual exhibition gates inside.
Very beautiful and stunning. The center of the world according to the Ming and Qing dynasties. Crowded but large enough to not feel it too much.

Forbidden city. This place needs no introduction. A must visit in Beijing. Highly recommended to book a local private guide. Saves you a lot of time from queueing - they will arrange for a striaght through service for you, and more importantly, a complete experience with detailed explanation of the museum. A must-do, must-do.

This is one of the top tourist attractions in Beijing. My visit to the palace museum was during winter and it was a different vibe out there with snow covered roofs and ground. You must take a note of the fact that before visiting the palace you must prebook a ticket at least 12 hours in advance and an adult ticket will cost only 7 dollars. They don’t encourage ticket issuing on premises. The palace museum marks the history of 24 emperors during the Ming and Qing dynasties. Also you should take note of the fact palace museum is located within the forbidden city and at present a visit to forbidden city == visit to the palace museum. If you are an history enthusiast i would recommend borrowing a voice guide. But if you are here for some stunning pictures then you can manage all by yourself. For the youth it has become a trend to wear like chinese princes and princesses before entering the palace.

The palace itself is stunning, just like everyone here is mentioning and you can see on pics. 1 star less for the very complicated and long process to get in… plan additional 1hr to buy ticket and get through countless security checks. Also after exiting, you will need to walk 30min to get to an area where a taxi can actually pick you up

Grand palace steeped in history, wished we had more time to enjoy it. The architecture, thought and details were amazing. The palace grounds were vast, the stories aplenty. The red palace walls juxtaposed against the white snow was beautiful. Rent an audio guide at least or you will miss plenty of information about the antiquities and history of the Dynasties. Probably need a full day and a half just to visit every building within. Not much food to find within the palace grounds, do make sure you have a meal before you enter if you plan to visit. The Palace Museum is a must visit, will return again someday!

The palace museum is the "world's largest palace by area enclosed within the palace's fortified walls" is held by China's Forbidden city complex in Beijing, which covers an area of 728,000 square metres (180 acres). The 980 buildings of the Forbidden City have a combined floor space of 1,614,600 square feet (150,001 m2) and contain 9,999 rooms (the ancient Chinese believed the god Yu Huang had 10,000 rooms in his palace; so they constructed an earthly palace to have 9,999 and a half rooms, slightly fewer than in the divine palace, out of respect). In this place you would drift into the time of the Chinese imperial dynasty at the beginning of the middle of the century if you were a colossal war filmmakers. One of the places you're obliged to go if you walk down the street to China. At an affordable ticket price, a clean, well-kept place with the canals surrounding the palace. This place is so amazing.👍👍

This is a fascinating place to visit. Many young ladies were celebrating the aesthetics of the Qing Dynasty, characterized by elaborate silk robes and ornate hairpieces - very beautiful. The entrance procedure is very complicated however for an international traveller as you need to book through a website which is often not attainable. Do not book your tickets through Agoda or Viator! My booking reference was not recognised at the gate. Fortunately the booking clerk at the Meridian Gate allowed me to pay for an official ticket on the day.

Definitely a must visit if you are in Beijing. Tickets should be reserved in advance as they only admit 80,000 guests per day and tickets are splits into a 8am entry or 12pm entry. Its like entering a movie set. The buildings and grounds are spectacular. Allow yourself at least 4 hours to enjoy the views explore the grounds and take plenty of photos.

Absolutely stunning palace, art installation and fascinating history. Buying ticket in advance is absolutely recommended. I was able to get ticket through the WeChat mini program The Palace Museum for up to 4 adults. Make sure to bring your ID and be prepared to walk!!

Booking is required 7 days in advance. We used a travel agent, Klook, but you can also book directly through the government website. We took a taxi to the site, and the closest allowable drop off area (Nanheyyan Ave and East Changan Ave) was quite far from the Meridien Gate, around a 20min walk. If you take a subway to Tiananmen (exit A) it is closer around a 15 min walk. After you exit the subway, you will need to show your passport a few times to security. I had visited the Forbidden City over 20 years ago, and things have changed considerably. The crowds are ten times the size from my memory, and a few of the buildings were closed off. Despite the crowds and heavy rain, it was still an enjoyable visit, and our guide was knowledgeable and friendlly, explaining a lot of detail that is not found on the sign boards or audio guides. It took around 2-3 hours but easily could have lasted longer, but we were soaked and cold from the rain. The exit is north of the palace so plan your next site accordingly. Taxi pickups far from the gate exit, around a 15 min walk.

This is probably one of the most famous landmarks in Beijing. The historic and cultural significance of this place makes this without a doubt, a must visit place for any tourist. The sprawling grounds that are opened to visitors are quite well kept considering the age and massive amounts of human traffic. We engaged an official guide, not one of the touts standing around, and had a blast listening to the various stories as we walked around. For the unfamiliar, a guide is the way to go, as the place is huge, and you get to ask questions. We spent nearly a full day there, and had to still skip some of the exhibitions inside that requires payment. Yes, on top of the entrance fee, there are exhibitions here and there that requires a small fee as well. Don't be daunted by the tight security, and massive crowds, as this is really one of those places you have to see at the very least once in your life.

Amazing place! Don't pay for the audio tour, it is really crappy. Pay a guide better! Start with Tiananmen park first, or it is really far once you finish the Forbidden City to come back, as entrance is closed for exiting. There are plenty of restaurant on your way out. It will take you around two hours for a quick tour. Enjoy this wonder!

This must visit place in Beijing, more crowded place.. Make reservations before you reach the place. The Forbidden City was constructed from 1406 to 1420, and was the former Chinese imperial palace and winter residence of the Emperor of China from the Ming ... Built: 1406–1420 (Ming dynasty) Location: 4 Jingshan Front St, Dongcheng, Beijing, China

A must visit attraction in Beijing, as it is the palace, center of China’s capital. There you can see the home that belonged to generations of emperors, its astonishing architecture and culture. Though, keep in mind that it is usually crowded inside, cling to your relatives/friends or you might get lost.

Is not the Forbidden City a Wonder of the World? It's one of the few places in the world, like Petra and le Mount St Michel, that blew me away so much that I had to sit down to take it all in. Stunning architecture, incredible craftsmanship and then a fascinating history to back it all. It's worth visiting Beijing just for this. Tickets are inexpensive, and unlike everywhere else in Beijing they were relatively easy to get. The official website, which you can google, is in English and can supply you with an email to show at the ticket office. Entrance to the Forbidden City is via Tiananmen Square. Walk through the tunnel under Mao's portrait and keep walking. You'll need a ticket for Tiananmen Square too. I read that if you have a Forbidden City ticket you don't need one for the square, but I got one anyway to be safe, as they are free. Ask your hotel to book one for you. If all else fails, just turn up and flash your passport. Nobody checked our ticket at security.

This place is so much bigger than I had imagined. You will want to get here early and spend the entire day walking through the grounds. Wear comfortable shoes. I definitely recommend the audio tour. There are special exhibits that cost a little extra but the cost is small compared to what you get to see. Truly an experience! You buy tickets in the right corner near the entrance gate. Please be sure to bring your passport with you. You should carry it at all times when you are in a foreign country.

Incredible details in the architecture, furniture, and artifacts. Paying extra for the museum is worth it. They have moved most of the collections from the main building over to the museum. The windows in the main part make it hard to see and appreciate the decorations, but the museum let's you go inside and get a close look.

One of the best historical place I've ever been, it's a must visit spot for anyone who will be visiting Beijing, if you could, go on weekdays, avoid China's national holiday in September and China's summer holiday, weekends because the place will be too crowded, or you would be watching people at every turns on each side of you instead of anything else. There are a lot of walking involved because the place was incredibly huge. Like most other main tourist attractions in Beijing, it is closed on every Monday so you need to plan your journey before visiting. About the entrance tickets, it is not available for sale on spot. The easiest, cheapest and safest way for foreigners to purchase tickets would be to send an email to the official palace museum website's email with information including your passport number, name and date to book the tickets within the seven days before you visit the Palace museum. You can find the email on the ENGLISH official palace museum website, you won't find the email and this booking method if you navigate to the Chinese language section of the official website, this option is only available for non-chinese people/tourists to book tickets to the palace museum. Once you received the email reply from the palace museum officers, you only need to go to the ticket counter at the palace museum on spot and show them your passport and email screenshot to get your tickets. You can pay the tickets with any payment methods. The easiest way to survive in China is to get a China phone number and download alipay app, then you can pay for anything with the QR code in the alipay app, including the subway and bus.🤗 You should also bring an empty booklet where you can get free stamp ink seals that are truly memorable for collection. The palace museum is a must visit place!✨ There are historical clothes rental shops nearby the place where you can rent the clothes and wear them into the place for a more immersive historical travel experience. Experience the beautiful palace where the ancient emperor lived thousands years ago❤️ also, don't forget to try the delicious and wonderful afternoon dessert set served by the cafe in the palace museum😋 especially the lychee soup. Legend has it that the empress ate it✨

The Palace Museum or "Forbidden City" is an absolutely massive complex (the maps do not do it justice) of stunningly detailed historic Chinese architecture built for royalty. It mainly consists of a number of massive courtyards, with similar huge buildings along the central axis, and a series of smaller courtyards to ether side each with a slightly different feel and architectural style. It is a one way tour, as you can ONLY access the complex through the southern gates and exit through the northern gates, but once in you can explore at will (although much easier to move with the huge crowds than against them). You don't need to book this as a trip through a tour guide, as it's perfectly easy to do yourselves, but please remember to bring your passport as a foreigner or you WON'T GET IN!!

This is a huge complex with a helpful audio guide. 4 stars because one employee told us that we couldn’t book same day tickets. However when we went to the ticket window it turned out to be no problem.

Such an amazing experience just getting to walk through this place. Each corridor, or wing, or even each palace held so much history and just left me in awe through out the entire day. Now the little petty cab that took us back to our hotel completely ripped us off, but it was a learning experience.

An important historical landmark. The Royal palace is very large. I'd recommend either hiring a guide or joining a tour group as you won't really know what you are looking at without some commentary as it's vast and a lot of the buildings and structures look similar. Most of the buildings you can't go inside or there's not much to see.
One of the most scrutinize place on earth especially getting the square under extreme cold weather. Security is top notch and the forbidden city is like walking into a movie set. Impressive.

If you visit Beijing, this is a must to go! Advance ticket required and you must reserve the ticket via official website only. Suggest buying a morning ticket if you can planned ahead. No ticket no entry normally. Except during low seasons (Nov-Mar) as it's cold and freezing months (but avoid Chinese lunar new year for all parts of china believe me...I bet it was too packed to deal with..haha) If the registered visitor has less than 80,000 paxes. Passport needed to verify to enter if you've got a ticket, just present your passport with the officer. If you love a historical story it takes a day for a walk but if you have short visit times, 2.5-3 hours is great for main sites.

You must bring your passport and try to avoid bringing a backpack. Visits can only be made through designated entrances. We bought the morning tour through the Trip.com app; otherwise, it would have been difficult to get the admission tickets. Only certain areas are open to visitors.

Great museum and temple. Architecture is stunning. Normal time to stay in is 3 hours, if you want to see every palace maybe more time. You need to separate tickets with some days in advance since the only thing they accept at entrance is your ID or passport/Visa number.

History to me is amazing and there is plenty of history to be found in China. We tried taking the self guided tour but do not recommend it. Take the tour and listen to the guide they make the trip much more enjoyable. If in Beijing I suggest you at least enjoy a stroll through just to take some amazing pictures.

It’s beautiful. It’s really big and also going to be full of people no matter when you go. Tip: buy the ticket online. I did through trip advisor. I was given a code on my phone. But at the entrance the staff just looked at my passport. They entered my number into their machines and saw our tickets. Tip 2: if you’re not with a guide, rent an audio to guide it costs 40CNY (~$6). It knows what room/area you’re in and plays once you’re within the vicinity.

It wasn't caked the Forbidden City for nothing... Opulence at its grandest... In the heart of Beijing. Its a must see!! Expect to spend at least half a day inside of you want to get a good understanding of the place. One can buy tickets at the counter on the left just before the entrance, by showing your passport... Wasn't trouble at all.

Amazing palace. Covering such a large area, there is so much to see. I was there for over 4 hours and still didn't see everything. There are many small museums located inside. So many people, but a must visit.

Must-see in Beijing, with newly opened to the public areas, so that I can enjoy the old places with new perspectives. You can see lots of traces of erosion weathering and decay, and some of the rooms I used to be able to step in when I was young are no longer available, but still there's no doubt you can get a glimpse of old glory and majesty. Make sure you hydrate during the summer time. There is a fancy little cafe on westside of north gate, where you can relax while sipping some good coffee.

This places gives a full history of Chinese culture, both in terms of architecture and custom. It is super interesting and is very well done, in terms of the signage and information. We did not have a guide and were able to still fully enjoy the experience and learn about the different buildings, of which there were many. The space is huge, mind boggling that the area takes up such a huge area - it goes on and on and on. A must see if you are in Beijing.

This place is packed with so much history it could take a couple days to let it all soak in. Certain places with the palace are off limits to cameras and others are off limits due to construction when I last visited. You can get guided tours by tape recorder or in person in your own language. The architecture and the fine details put into each and every thing within the walls of this city within a city. After all it was designed to keep the elite members of society from ever leaving as it was so beautiful. Truly stunning and a must see. Another item off the bucket list here as well folks. I loved my trip so much that my parents decided to come and see it for themselves. I cannot get enough of the people and culture here that i have to come back again and again

The Palace Museum and Forbidden City is a massive tourist location with thousands of visitors that come to these spots every day. The Forbidden City is in very good condition and you can tell its been very well maintained over the years. My only warning is to be prepared for the swarms of people. We didn't notice it as much as first, but about halfway through our time of visiting the forbidden city, the police/military officials started closing off about two thirds of the museum forcing all of the tourist to go through only small parts of the City. We felt like we weren't able to see most of the city because daily closure. But we enjoyed the parts of the city that we were able to see.

Obviously incredible...go early to attempt to avoid crowds! Take passport with you...you'll need to use it for both security check and as your 'ticket' once you pay. No clear information about that on location and when you are used to receiving a paper ticket it can be a little unnerving.

I will advice anyone that wants to come here to come here during the down season. THIS PLACE IS PACKED WITH PEOPLE, we came during a summer season and it was almost unberable, there are people everywhere you go, Bring lots of drinks and maybe a towel . EXPECT TO DO A LOT OF WALKING, otherwise this place is beautiful, but knocking one star off the rating as they really have poor crowd control. enter the museum and exit on the other end,

A historical location that's definitely worth visiting. Full of history and will definitely catch your interest. Please remember to buy your tickets online! You can't but tickets on site. One set back is that the place is very very crowded. It does not feel like an ant line but more like a swarm of bees crowding around a nest!!! Psychologically, please be prepared. You can see the photos to get a feel of the crowd. Enjoy😄
Even is weekday still have many people went to visit. Highly recommended book the guided tour.It can help you to understand the history of The Palace Museum.

One of the highlights of Beijing and a must do for tourists. Takes about an hour or more to get through but is definitely worth the walk. It is interesting to see the scale of this palace and to imagine how many generations have seen this. It is a very important piece of history and you can certainly feel that.

Really impressive. Its my second time here but I am still amazed at how big and beautiful this palace is. This historic place is unique, huge and beautiful. If you are into China History, it’s strongly recommended.
Love this place. I visited during the golden week, was pretty packed but still enjoyed walking through the palace very much.

This place is amazing. It take you back in time. It is a bit confusing where to get tickets form and that could be quite stressful since they have a visitors cap each day. Be prepared to walk a lot and allocate over 4 hours for a complete tour of the palace. We did the audio tour and we truly enjoyed it. Probably the best thing to do in Beijing.

Exceptional, grandious, and so well preserved!! Bring your passport, you'll need it to access the forbidden city. Recommended to take the audio guide, self activated when approaching main spots and useful to orientate in such a big area, it marks where you are by lighting leds. Count a minimum of 4 hours going fast including western and eastern palaces.
Put aside a while day for the visit to the forbidden city. Pick a few museums you wish to see, take your time. Bring a friend speaking chienese.

This is one of the best palace buildings I think. The place where the ancient Chinese emperors lived and worked. Spring, summer, autumn and winter will have different scenery in different seasons. This is the charm of the Forbidden City. In this city, you can also see a lot of ancient handicrafts, works of various masters.

Gorgeous even during winter. Take the leisurely stroll to enjoy the grounds. If you have time, don't miss the marble boat amd the back lakes. Went for dim sum lunch at the Arman Hotel on the grounds. Over priced and not up to par.

I can't imagine anyone rating less than 5 stars to this magnificent masterpiece of historical architecture. The Forbidden City indeed worths the flight to Beijing from anywhere in the world. Take your time there, and don't forget that there is much more to see than "just" the main temples in the center: don't miss to visit the alleys and the little temples placed East and West! The City was not only inhabited by the emperor, but by plenty of people who were living their everyday lives. Tip: take some food with you because the restaurant inside really sucks. I believe the emperor was not a trusted customer there.

Very beautiful with so many things to see. We were not very accustomed to the pushing and shoving that accompanied the massive crowds. It was chaos trying to get our bag into the x-ray scanner. By the time we got in we were both in bad moods so only stayed for a little while. It is something that must be seen when in Beijing though.
Unimaginable ancient city still in well kept condition. Most building interiors are bare with just the structures to see. We bought tickets on site with no queues.

Buy tickets in advance and bring your passport. Lots of people, lots to see. Very little sitting options. Bring comfortable shoes. No shades or trees, hot in summer. Recommended for the history fanatics.

Great experience, If you are foreigners then getting tickets can be tricky. Online booking site is in Chinese and like most of the places they accept Card issued in China 🇨🇳 or you need wechat account with payment enabled. I asked my colleague to book tickets i paid them cash. Also remember, you need to book the tickets in advance like 1 or 2 days before. Daily capacity for this place is close to 80000 still you won't get tickets for same day. Its very huge place and you will need at least 4 to 5 hours. I was there for couple of hours. Make sure yiu carry passport, they didn't ask at security but its recommend.
The magnificent Forbidden City, the palace of the emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties of China. Visiting here requires advance booking, with limited daily sales.

It's may take all day for you to visit and took pictures because forbidden city is so very big, beautiful and impressive, you should buy ticket beforehand on klook it's easier for you to go check in by your passport number, you can buy ticket for treasure hall and clock hall before or when you came there. I think it is beautiful the most in spring many kind of flower make it so romantic

It was snowing. First day of snow in Chinese New Year 2019 Beijing, on the first day that the Forbidden City Palace Museum was open for the year and last day of our wintery vacation in Beijing. It was crowded with people which was surprising and we couldn't locate a ticket area for the vast place. We did get a few really good pics and then left after walking around for about 1.5 hours and took a taxi back to our hotel once we walked a mile out to avoid traffic congestion. On an off note, the taxis asked us for more money to return to hotel then when the hotel ordered us a taxi, coming to and from same location. This happened on 2 separate occasions. Seemed dishonest but was still a cool trip.

100% worth a visit when in Beijing! Wear comfortable shoes, bring sunglasses and dress warmly if visiting in winter. The upside of visiting the Forbidden City during COVID times is most definitely the lack of a crowd. Daily visitor numbers are capped so there is none of the pre-COVID shoulder-to-shoulder crowding situation. The downside is that you cannot wake up and decide to go as tickets must be pre-booked via the Wechat mini app at least a day in advance. For entry: It is a must to bring your original ID (not a scan or photo of it) in order to gain entry. Guide: We rented an audio guide for 20rmb (in Chinese) which comes with a ear piece. The cool thing about the guide is that 1) it has the entire map of the Forbidden City printed on its front side + it automatically starts talking when it senses the building you are walking to. Audio guides in foreign languages are available too for 40rmb. There might be some human guides hanging about near the audio guide rental place and they charge between 150-300rmb for a tour. Might be good for history enthusiasts who want a detailed tour (and who speak Chinese!) Food: There are two very reasonable priced Chinese restaurants inside the Forbidden City. One is located in the middle and the other is near the exit. We visited the one in the middle of the attraction and really enjoyed the black bean paste noodles (炸酱面). Each main course costs between 40-60rmb. Souvenirs: The last and largest souvenir shop is located near the exit (in the Imperial Garden 御花园). Highly recommend going in and checking out the items that they have, even if you don’t want to buy anything. Most of the souvenirs are beautifully designed and very affordable! Overall duration: We found it nearly quite impossible to finish the entire attraction in one sitting. We went in early Dec for the third time and still thoroughly enjoyed our visit. For estimates, we arrived at 11am and left at about 5pm.

Really fascinating buildings and history, but VERY crowded. Need to book tickets in advance, online OR go via an organised tour. The Chinese need ID to access the site, foreigners need their passports or national ID. A bit run-down in parts which surprised me. Huge site, well worth a visit, just be prepared for vast crowds. Not good for people of limited mobility though, as there are lots of steps and uneven paving.
Amazing experience. It was my first time and blew my mind with how massive and beautiful the city is. Huge bonus: they had dragons, so if you like those, this is a must see.

Absolutely incredible piece of history. Must visit if you are interested in Chinese history and arts. The palace museum is very grand and would probably require half a day to walk through. The electronic map audio guide was especially helpful and educational. For the tickets, either join a tour group or have local friends help you out; otherwise you might not be able to get in on the day. Get tickets before your actual visit. If you don’t enjoy crowds, think twice before coming. Our group visited on a week day but there were many local tourists that have absolutely no manner. Prepared to be shoved aside; the locals apparently do not understand the concept of getting in line. Security check was chaotic. Going to the washroom could be a huge challenge for the ladies. Even our Chinese friends (city Shanghai gals) were quite freaked out by those visitors’ rude behavior. Try to use the washrooms inside the palace, and not at the entrance and exit. There is also a cafe by the palace museum. The pricing is high (similar to Starbucks), but they offer really neat coffee cup design; good experience. If only the museum could do a better job organizing the crowd, I would definitely rate it a five star. It felt odd to see modern shops within the palace; those should be separated from the original structure...
Amazing really!!! You need to have a guide in order to get the full experience!!!! Very difficult to book the ticket on your own. You need 3 hours more or less. Bring your passport!!!!

You need to buy the ticket a week in advance. You cannot visit inside the rooms anymore, so it’s pointless to visit without someone explaining the history and meaning of each place. The place was extremely crowded, and areas have been closed/restricted recently since the pandemic.

The scope is massive and size not to be underestimated. We were there 5-6 hours and skipped a lot. There is a small entry fee of a few dollars with extra exhibits costing extra here and there. Minus 1 point because the audioguide was flaky and only worked half the time and because there were multiple exhibits being restored that you could not see or enter (probably for next year's expo) and because it was difficult to see exhibits inside the buildings. Usually resulting in a scramble of selfie sticks near the one open window/door. Tip 1:. They will ask for your passports as a non national. Multiple times. In some exhibits, your passport is a kind of ticket. You pay entrance fee and then it's assigned to your passport number. They then enter that passport number into a computer at the checkpoint and if it's flagged as "paid' then you can go inside. Tip 2: no toilet paper in bathrooms, plan accordingly. Mostly squatter toilets. Tip 3:. There is a restaurant and some food vendors inside. They are not common though and can get crowded. We paid about 30-40 ¥ each for a good lunch there. My wife is German so she knew how to grab a table in a crowded restaurant ;) Tip 4:. If you plan your visit around a clear day (check visibility forecast) and have left over energy after you exit from the north gate, then you can walk up another park and have an amazing view of the forbidden city that you just visited.

A total of 24 generation of rulers were ruling China from this place. For foreigners it’s a must to carry passport to be provided with an entrance ticket. We entered into the palace by 8:30 and the colors that could not be missed are the red and yellow as the whole place is covered in them. The exit of the palace is at the back so the crowd has only one direction of flow reducing the congestion of the pouring tourists.

One of the best place to learn the history of China, it a long walk but all is worth it. You see lot of the old furnitures and different ornament of the olden days, you will have an idea of how things work work in the past. Also learn how the other countries invaded the palace and how they looted some stuff from the Qing government. Very good walk and very good learning experience.

Forbidden palace is a place that you would not want to miss. This place is filled with history of several emperor's. Over here, you could see well preserved architecture and be amazed that all these structures are build without using a single nail yet it survived numerous earthquakes. If you are like me, who get attracted to the rich history and would like to take time to really look through the place. I suggest you take a day to visit the place and probably during a weekday whereby there might be lesser tourist. In the forbidden city itself, there's eatery and cafe. Of course, delicate souvenirs are sold there for you to bring home a memory. And you would see pretty China teenagers, dress up in ancient costume and snapping photos. If you're up for it, you can get a set of the costume in any store outside and try it yourself. Because why not?

Very good place to visit and reasonable entry price, free if 60 or over. Some sections inside require seperate entry fee. Some locals may want to take picture with you as they did with me. The locals are very friendly. There are plenty of well kept and free toilets and it is kept clean, with none of the littering in some countries. Plenty of bins both for recycling and other rubbish available I went on a hot day but luckily lots of shaded places

Very good museum. They have discount for students with ISIC. My suggestion after crossing ticket check go upstairs and walk along deffensive walls. At each corner tower done exhibition is presented. It is much more interesting than walk through inner years. They are very similar. You will be bored very fast 🤫. Must visit in Beijing!

You will walk a lot !! The place is amazing, somehow crowded but if you divert from the people flow you can enjoy some calm, I went on the ladders that take you to the walls and was basically by myself, you can see how big is the city from there, if you follow the crowd be prepared, it is seriously crowded, kids may enjoy it for maybe an hour, after that is too much for them, plan to spend at least 3-4 hours, arrived early you won’t regret it, and don’t forget your passport, that will be your ticket !

Definitely a must visited stop in Beijing. Only take your time to do your research and buy tickets in advance to avoid lines. Also, better to be informed about what to see. There is alot to look at and it can be tiring.

First of all there is no good food there so therefore better prepare your own food!! It’s a very touristy place and there is a lot of people most of the time but it’s really huge so there will always be some corners here and there that you will not meet anyone. Personally I like nature and therefore I do not find anything interesting in this forbidden palace because it looks the same to me everywhere. For someone who is into architecture and history, it is probably a good place to spend some time. You don’t get to go inside the rooms and the palace though.

Amazing place. It is once in a lifetime experience! China has a greaat hisatorical legacy. The Palace Museum, also known as the Forbidden City is kept immaculately. It is inexpensive for a ticket, and even more so if you're a senior.

Come early in the morning right when the gates open! If you're lucky you may be able to see much of the square with only a few people. The museum is nothing to write home about (as they're mostly in the British natural history museum). Come for the structures, history; be sure to check out the 7 dragon wall and the concubine well. Afterwards climb the mountain on the north side for a scenic view of the palace.
Tight security and advice to purchase the ticket in advance and do expect a long queue to enter the forbidden city. You can spend at least 4 hours to really explore the whole place.

A Historic Places one should must visit when he/she goes to Beijing. If you visit here during Winters make sure you cover yourself completely as this place is too windy. You will find antiques all over, great place for seeing creativity.

An amazing historic site with beautiful gardens and buildings. It may take a while to get inside but it’s well worth the wait, there are also a number of other interesting historic sites near by. There is also a train station close by so getting there is very easy.

The forbidden city is a good place to see the royal palace of China since the early 15th century and to understand the palace architecture that has a much longer history. The symmetric design, the yellow and red colors, the number nine, the zoomorphic throne of dragon……All these are quite Chinese, let’s say. Of course, the administrative compound in the front and the living quarter in the back remind me the topqapi palace in Istanbul.

The one thing you want to visit if you are travelling in Beijing. This majestic ancient palace is breathtaking. It is the ancient palace of the emperor and you can easily spend 3-4 hours inside. The tickets can be bought online (Chinese website -- you will need AliPay or a Chinese Bank Card) or on-site (only for foreigners in small booths on the right before the entrance). The price is 60 yuan + 10 yuan for the jewelry museum (lots of ancient treasures belonging to the emperor) +10 yuan for the clock museum (lots of impressive and various clocks offered by different nations to China). There is a restaurant inside next to the clock museum which is often crowded.

The forbidden city is one of the most spectacular sites in China. It's huge, you can spend days exploring what they let you. Structures are incredible, scale hard to imagine, history and culture one of a kind.

The forbidden city covers a huge area and invites visitors to enjoy the various exhibitions and small parks. Best bring some food and find a nice place to enjoy the view and have a picknick. The audio guide provides some information and stories for a few spots, so it does not get boring. Some exhibitions charge an tiny extra fee, which in my opinion is worth it. Chinese can order their tickets online one day in advance others have to get what's left from the small office before the inner gates. Don't go an weekends or holidays, probably tickets will be sold out and the place is totally overcrowded.

To be honest, I found the Forbidden City quite underwhelming. The buildings pretty much all look the same and most are closed off to the public from getting too close to see inside. The interesting parts cost more money to see and the incessant hoards of crowds makes it a quite unpleasant experience. It might have just been the fact that Chinese tourists themselves seem to litter everywhere and spit on their own national treasure. Why they would do that to such a beautiful piece of history is beyond me. If you can ignore the crowds, you will find some really interesting architecture though it takes a bit of a walk to get around. Don't bother with the self guided electronic tour - I had to change mine three times before it worked and even then it didn't play for me at some of the sites so I just gave up on it. Don't expect to see any historical relics or descriptions of historic life or anything like that. It really is just crowds and a bunch of buildings to take selfies in front of.

Access is challenging but well worth the effort! The forbidden city is fantastic but getting there was confusing. We had to show passports to enter Tiananmen Square first (access is free, just follow the crowds through security scans). Following the crowds in the square we ended up entering the mausoleum, which didn't really interest us. Finally found the entrance to the Forbidden city, there are signs to buy tickets online but there is also an office to buy with cash (again you need your passport for this). The Palace Museum is amazing, very long walks along stunning buildings and the imperial gardens at the end (north) are truly wonderful.

Be prepared to do a bit a waiting through checks and everything to get in. For a ticket your best bet would be to arrange with your hotel to prebook one online and than you only have to show your passport to get in at the final check. Sounds weird but it works! Inside it's huge area, where you can walk around for a good 2-3 hours. Definitely worth it though.

On the website, it shows that 75000 people are allowed to make reservation to get in here per day, and this palace is extremely huge, which makes me think that it will not be crowed, and I was wrong. Also, some of the visitors suggest to make a reservation, but in my opinion it is not necessary, just wait in line and purchase ticket is fine, since the line of getting your reservation ticket are long too. Lots of people, but the ancient palace is totally worth seeing.

The Forbidden City itself is huge and can be a slow burn due to the mass of people. It is definitely worth seeing once, but I would suggest it is a one time thing. I suppose without crowds it would be better. I heard from the locals that it is MUCH quieter during the winter and so I'd suggest timing your trip accordingly if possible. Whilst there, I witnessed at least three occasions where mother's would drop the trousers of their children and let them defecate on the floor of the Forbidden City. My advice would be watch where you step.

Very very big. Getting inside took a little while because of the massive crowds, but once you're in it's well worth the wait. If you go during the summer, bring a sun shade since there isn't much shade. Also doesn't hurt to bring water yourself. There are plenty of vendors that you can buy water from, but you'll go through a lot. They have a great automatic tour guide that is in English which helps. You can literally spend hours here. Rich in history and amazing sights to see.

Amazing place, the history here is just great, we were lucky and it wasn't crowded so was a great experience to go here. Just to look all what happened here and see an amazing landmark by yourself I have to say it's a check mark you most have been done.
An interesting place to visit, high on the list of things to do for travelers to Beijing. Lots of information to take in, but can also just walk around and admire the architecture.

This is a top tourist attraction in Beijing. Tourist from around the world as well as Chinese from other parts of the country used to visit. This is too big inside. Similar structures are there one after the other.

Don't take a set tour that just walks you through the palace. There are many fascinating rooms and museums off to the sides that the tours skip. You need most of a day to do the Palace correctly. Well worth the time.

I feel sheepish writing a review about such a culturally/globally significant location as The Forbidden City. I mean- these buildings are older than my country. I had previously experienced the splendor of The Imperial Palace vicariously through film- “The Last Emperor” easily the most notable among them. The expanse is even more impressive when you consider that these buildings were constructed on human labor alone. It should go without saying that if you’re ever in Beijing, then this is a must for stops on your journey.

I've had the chance to visit it multiple times as just once is not enough. It can take a lot of time to visit and thoroughly enjoy the place. Going in early is the best way to avoid the crowds and I always finish my visit by going on top of the hill when you exit the city to have a breath taking view of it.

Visiting palace museum can be an uneasy task as they are trying to regulate number of visitors per day. I tried to book the tickets a day before, but I didn't got any text message from the online booking system (I don't have chinese phone number). So I went without a ticket and wanted to buy it on spot. But this is not so easy, because you can only exchange the online ticket for a paper one in the booths. So I had to find somebody nice enough (this is not a problem, but they usually don't speak a word in English) to order a ticket online, pay with alipay (or something similar), get a cash from me and exchange the online ticket for paper one in one of the booths. In total it took me around half an hour to get in. It is huge inside so people diffuse in the volume and you can find even abandoned places inside.

A vast and huge palace. Beautiful architecture and interesting history. It gets very busy so best to go early. If visiting without a organised tour, take your passport with you as that will be your entrance ticket.

Loved visiting the Forbidden City in Beijing. It is a very large area with over 8,000 buildings, so put on your walking shoes! L9ts of stairs too. There are a number of restaurants, shops and souvenir stands. Public toilets are few and far. Entry cost is 20RMB (about $3.50US) but only after you enter the main gate. You need to identify yourself for entry, so bring your passport. Lots of english translations. This is a beautiful reflection on Chinese history and culture. Well kept and patronised. I think it opens at 9am to 6pm...there is always less people in the mornings - so get up early and get going!

Great historical palace. Got there early so there weren't too many visitors buying tickets or blocking photo opportunities. The audio guide is highly recommended and made me appreciate the palace more with the historical knowledge.
Online reservation 1 week in advance is a must. They limit the visitors per day but it was still very crowded inside. Very hot during summer day. Restaurants available inside the premises.
Great historical site. It can get very busy so watch out for the crowds and pick pockets. There's a lot of walking so wear comfortable shoes and carry a water bottle.

Must-go place to visit in Beijing, China. Great place to explore the spectacular architecture and know about China history, Ming and Qing Dynasties. Better go in the early morning to avoid large crowd from the travel agencies’. The entrance fee varies between seasons, ¥60 from April to October, ¥40 from November to March. And they have audio guide device to rent at the entrance, make sure you have cash as they do not accept other payments.

You have not been to Beijing if you have not been inside the Forbidden City. With more than 400 years of history, a treasure to the present and future generations. Good to have a guide but even if you do not, the is a device u can rent for a self guided tour catered l Great value for money. Entrance fee is only RMB40 best bought conveniently through WeChat.

If the complex was intended to be a magnanimous display of power and wealth it does that with near grace a century later. The outdoor complex was Just stunning!! With massive courtyards for the king to greet a likely large adminstration / aristocratcy, housed symmetrical and proprtionate layout of building, the dragon art adorning the walls of each structures, and each building housed with hexangonal tiles on the inner roofs, saddle shaped golden / brown ceramic canopies, and red wooden walls brought the complex alive. And Yes, there is BUT - for me (maybe nitpicking here), the interior of the most rooms open for viewing didn't capture the imagination to the same extent as did the various courtyards. The glory of each room was lost either due to lack impact lighting, or glass and air-conditioning protection that could be employed to showcase to each visitor the glamor and pomp of the royal court / life. Some details - As a visitor .. First and foremost the complex is massive therefore be prepared with the right shoes, gear and drinks for hydration. Buy tickets early - online (for foreigners you may use websites like Klook and Viator for tickets or the hotel provided tour packages) or you may end stucks in long ques. E-tickets work at the entry gates. Recommend hiring a guide as the complex is vaste and some nibbles of knowledge shared can be interesting (based on our experience do some self research cuz our guide does skip or gloss over lots of relevant facts). Best starting point is Tinnammen Gate (if by train - exit at Tiannammen East train station) follow the crowds / lines towards The imposing Meridian Gate. A must do Once you have entered the gate make a right turn and find your way to the viewing decks (wall) of the meridian gate (note tour guides avoid this walk - insist you wish to see it we felt it was worth it). Upon Walking through the entire Palace complex and exit at the North gate and make time to visit Jingshan Park. The park has a great vantage view of the entire city (a visit near Sunset makes for a great photo opportunity). Overall a special visit!!
It's amazing place, huge and astonishing. definitely worth visiting while in Beijing. This place stores so much history.

Must see, despite all the masses a breathtaking place to visit. We bought the tickets directly at the meridian gate without preorder. There is a ticket booth on the right hand but please don't forget to have your password with you as it will serve as your ticket throughout the visit. Audioguides can be picked up after the meridian gate

Located off Tiananmen Square it is a no brainer to check this out, as well as Maos place of internment and other Beijing landmarks surrounding the square. Of course it is a cultural landmark, and essentially a must see, but it comes with buts. You MUST go as early as possible to avoid crowds (not truly possible but you can mitigate it some). Be forewarned the audible tour will be temperamental at best. IF you opt to get it do not be surprised to have it cut out mid sentence (happened on 3 devices our family had) and randomly restart working many minutes later. FYI I am convinced Joan Chen was one of the narrators. If you can opt for a private guide, by all means get one! As far as the sites, by sheer size it is an impressive compound. If you look with care you can find original paints and glazes used and imagine the structures in their full glory. Unfortunately some insane party chose some terribly garish colors to "decorate" the facades with and I am sorry but there is no way in hell those are historically accurate! Now as far as artifacts go, there are some collection scattered about the sprawling compound so you need to be on your toes to find those. There was an impressive collection clocks...yeah...not running tho, some looked quite animatronic in nature but left static. A weaponry collection, assorted ink drawings, paintings, illustrations, bronze works, etc. again scattered about. Many of the main meeting and throne rooms were quite adorned and looked to be spectacular but there was either no entrance for general observation or the only access wss from feet away from a few narrowly opened doorways with railing to keep you feet away which you could glance thru. Taking a photo, very challenging thru the throngs. Perhaps most stunning was the cavalcade of selfish stick wielders busy taking running movies of themselves showing the displays over their shoulders...opportunities to photobomb dolts abound! You can find some spectacular spots which are visually stunning but you have to do so purposefully. Towards the end of the forbidden City you will see the emperess & wives palaces which had many more exhibits housed in that section. The gardens at the end are fairly generic, but you will find bright spots as you look around. More pics to come not on cell phone.

This place is amazing! So many different rooms to see and decorations! The entrance fee is 60 RMB You will need your passport to be able to buy your entrance ticket, they will input your passport number into the system and this will be your ticket basically.
It's way too big. Inside there are extra things you have to pay to visit. The audio guides don't tell much. It was cool but maybe I was tired and it was difficult to find the exit

I think this is supposed to be a posting for the Forbidden City. I've been here a handful of times and I'm always just a bit underwhelmed. It's big. It's old. There's lots of history here. But the central line of touring which most of us spend our time on is pretty boring as they won't let you enter or even get close enough to really view what's inside. After the Forbidden City we went up to Jingshan Parkand we were able to witness how large the Forbidden City is once you leave that Central area. If I had explored those side areas maybe I would have higher praise. I have a friend who brings friends here to tour on a regular basis and she just takes them to Jing Shan Park which is only too quiet to enter and you get the great aerial view of the Forbidden city. it was more complicated to get in this we couldn't find a ticket booth and had to buy our tickets online. We did not get a tour guide because it more than doubled the price of the admittance but that may have helped the experience to be more interesting. As others have mentioned don't forget your passport and can't do anything in China, even get into free museums without your passport. if you really want to get an idea of how the emperor's lived go to the Summer palace. One of my favorite places.

Sprawling area with lots to cover. Make sure you can walk for a while without sitting down. Bathrooms are hard to find if even existent. I came on a "good air" day, but it was still smoggy. Interesting culture and history, but a little bland - similar to most temples/palaces/castles throughout Asia with the exception of Japan. You will get a lot of looks if you aren't Asian, and school children may talk to you - or be scared. You might be the first foreigner they ever have seen!

Words simply couldn’t describe the beauty of this place. The architecture the colours the name of the various gardens and palaces are just spectacular. Access could be a pain (long queue for passport checks) so try to go early and stay till sunset. It’s totally worth it at the end. I went in May but the palace is stunning in all season. Please prioritise this place while you are in Beijing!! There is also a restaurant inside serves really great roast duck. It’s called 冰窖 (Bing Jiao) where the imperial kitchen used to keep ice.

Probably one of the first things that come to mind when you say Beijing. It is "yuge" and it takes about 4-5 hours if you want to visit it entirely. They only let in a limited number of visitors at one time so i suggest you go there before noon to make sure you can enter. Better visit during weekdays as weekends are more crowded. They offer student discounts and they ask for passport upon issuing of tickets (no exceptions). If you have a student ID they will ask you if you are a bachelor, master or PhD student - make sure to say bachelor! They also have audio guides in about 20 languages. There are a few additional exhibitions inside (like the jewelry or clock exhibitions) for which you have to pay extra. Student discounts apply there also.
Absolutely amazing place but be ready as there is always a huge amount of people that is not easy to walk.......

In order to visit this place , you need to have knowledge of Dynasties of China. A historical place , the forbidden city, is surrounded by so many monuments and signs of prehistoric culture of The real China. A must visit place if you are traveling to Beijing. 👍👍👍

Always crouwded but must visit in Beijing. Early booking, early arrival to pass entry is the best safe tip. Not only the magnificent buildings but also different special exhibitions show the living style of people in both Ming & Ching dynasty.

It's ok to see it， especially if this is your first visit to China. A lot of temple buildings, you can't go into most of them. There arr to other temples you can see in China, where u can see more about the life of the era they represent. I recommend you go see Prince Teng Pavilion in Nanchang, same thing, only smaller, with a story and a view into theirs lives.

Pretty nice tourist area. There isn’t a huge variation in what you get to see, but of course the old Korean palatial housing is pretty beautiful. It’s well maintained and only a few thousand won to enter.

Beautiful chinese emperor palace that still preserved in good condition. Beautiful and grand architecture shows a reflection of how wealthy during the the the chinese dynasty of Ming and Qing where the emperors has stayed inside this beautiful palace. A huge square and can contains million of people in today context. Can’t assess into their palace like bedroom, hall but can only view from outside. The garden behind is as beautiful! Hard to imagine in thousand years ago such architecture can be built and last till today! Beautiful place to visit if you come to Beijing visit.

Great place, it will probably take someone to visit it at least 4 hours, although you could spend north of 8 hrs easily. Amazing stuff to see everywhere and the place is huge. Expect very big crowds though.

It is indeed a sight to behold. One could just stand in awe on how to wrap the mind around the splendour of the royal families who lived there thousands of years ago then, compared today, it's definitely something to ponder upon. Personally speaking, I would say they had quality back then, we have the internet now.

The forbidden palace is a must place to visit if youre in beijing but just keep in mind that tickets may be sold out. So buy tickets in advance or be there early also dont forget to bring your passport as you needed to enter the palace.

Very advisable to buy the ticket in advance as the limit of 80k visitors/day is reached several days in advance. The complex is big althought all buildings are repetitive. Good audio guide available at the entrance in several languages. Be prepared for big and unpleasant groups of people.

One fantastic piece of Beijing history is the Forbidden City. Surrounded by water it is a large part of the city sightseeing area. Full of temples and large areas with a fair amount of tourists. So many great buildings showing many of the techniques used in creating such a fantastic place.
The Imperial Palace is one of the must see sites in China. it might be a good idea to go with a guided group otherwise you may find yourself waiting in line to buy tickets for quite some time.

Lots of things to see around. Get a paid tour to explain the history and background is beneficial and provide a lot of insights. Half a day wont be enough to cover all grounds if you are very specific, but sufficient to cover the more prominent areas. There is a palace museum cafe that serves food, beverages and a few dessert on the menu.

Definitely a must see spot if u r in Beijing. It’s pretty crowded, but hey that’s Beijing. Majestic historical place, should suggest to buy tickets in advance. When I was there it was impossible to by a ticket at the entrance they were all sold out.
Great visit. Plan 4 hours min. Lots of places to find drinks etc inside. Make sure you enter from the north gate as there is a one way system, i.e. you cannot enter and exit from same gate.

I would give more stars but we weren't able to get in due to tickets being sold out and there's only a limited amount of people let in each day. We got there at 8:30 a.m. and were told the tickets were sold out. If you do go, dont do what we did and go during Chinese New Year, you will most likely have a better chance of getting in. Also, wear comfortable clothes and walking shoes. Lots of walking to get to the entrance.
The Forbidden City was amazing! Huge complex, very well maintained. Not too crowded in mid winter but must be extremely crowded in summer. Use side entrance!
Really beautiful place to walk around. Was very crowded in the middle of the week, but it’s so big, that it doesn’t feel too crowded. A must visit when in Beijing.

The Palace Museum is housed in the Forbidden City, the Chinese imperial palace from the Ming Dynasty to the end of the Qing Dynasty. It is located in the middle of Beijing, China. For almost five centuries, it served as the home of the Emperor and his household, and the ceremonial and political centre of Chinese government. Built from 1406 to 1420, the complex consists of 980 surviving buildings with 8,707 bays of rooms[7] and covers 720,000 square metres. The palace complex exemplifies traditional Chinese palatial architecture,[8] and has influenced cultural and architectural developments in East Asia and elsewhere. The Forbidden City was declared a World Heritage Site in 1987,[8] and is listed by UNESCO as the largest collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world.

When Hongwu Emperor's son Zhu Di became the Yongle Emperor, he moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing, and construction began in 1406 on what would become the Forbidden City. Construction lasted 14 years and required more than a million workers. Material used include whole logs of precious Phoebe zhennan wood (Chinese: 楠木; pinyin: nánmù) found in the jungles of south-western China, and large blocks of marble from quarries near Beijing.The floors of major halls were paved with "golden bricks" (Chinese: 金砖; pinyin: jīnzhuān), specially baked paving bricks from Suzhou. From 1420 to 1644, the Forbidden City was the seat of the Ming dynasty. In April 1644, it was captured by rebel forces led by Li Zicheng, who proclaimed himself emperor of the Shun dynasty.He soon fled before the combined armies of former Ming general Wu Sangui and Manchu forces, setting fire to parts of the Forbidden City in the process. By October, the Manchus had achieved supremacy in northern China, and a ceremony was held at the Forbidden City to proclaim the young Shunzhi Emperor as ruler of all China under the Qing dynasty. The Qing rulers changed the names on some of the principal buildings, to emphasise "Harmony" rather than "Supremacy", made the name platesbilingual (Chinese and Manchu), and introduced Shamanist elements to the palace. In 1860, during the Second Opium War, Anglo-French forces took control of the Forbidden City and occupied it until the end of the war. In 1900 Empress Dowager Cixi fled from the Forbidden City during the Boxer Rebellion, leaving it to be occupied by forces of the treaty powers until the following year. After being the home of 24 emperors – 14 of the Ming dynasty and 10 of the Qing dynasty – the Forbidden City ceased being the political centre of China in 1912 with the abdication of Puyi, the last Emperor of China. Under an agreement with the new Republic of China government, Puyi remained in the Inner Court, while the Outer Court was given over to public use, until he was evicted after a coup in 1924. The Palace Museum was then established in the Forbidden City in 1925.In 1933, the Japanese invasion of China forced the evacuation of the national treasures in the Forbidden City.Part of the collection was returned at the end of World War II,but the other part was evacuated to Taiwan in 1948 under orders by Chiang Kai-shek, whose Kuomintang was losing the Chinese Civil War. This relatively small but high quality collection was kept in storage until 1965, when it again became public, as the core of the National Palace Museum in Taipei. After the establishment of the People's Republic of China in 1949, some damage was done to the Forbidden City as the country was swept up in revolutionary zeal.During the Cultural Revolution, however, further destruction was prevented when Premier Zhou Enlai sent an army battalion to guard the city. The Forbidden City was declared a World Heritage Site in 1987 by UNESCO as the "Imperial Palace of the Ming and Qing Dynasties",due to its significant place in the development of Chinese architecture and culture. It is currently administered by the Palace Museum, which is carrying out a sixteen-year restoration project to repair and restore all buildings in the Forbidden City to their pre-1912 state. In recent years, the presence of commercial enterprises in the Forbidden City has become controversial. A Starbucks store that opened in 2000 sparked objections and eventually closed on 13 July 2007.Chinese media also took notice of a pair of souvenir shops that refused to admit Chinese citizens in order to price-gouge foreign customers in 2006. On November 8, 2017, President of the United States Donald Trump was the first US President to be granted a state dinner in the Forbidden City since the founding of the People's Republic of China...
